$comment: Each entry names a publisher and its canonical public skill directory. additionalPaths lists other public skill directories in the same repository. Catalog editions are distinct by credited author. Reprints by the same author use the first canonical source. revision pins a reviewed collection to an exact Git commit. skillPaths imports only the listed Markdown-only skill folders.

sources.author: Jesse Vincent
sources.bundleNote: Superpowers skills are written to work together — using-superpowers teaches the agent when to reach for the rest — so the full set gets the most out of any one of them.

sources.author: Corey Haines
sources.bundleNote: These skills build on shared context: every one of them reads product-marketing first for your product, audience, and positioning, so install product-marketing alongside whichever you pick.

sources.author: Google Workspace CLI
sources.bundleNote: Many Workspace recipes use the shared gws-shared skill and a service-specific skill. Install the Workspace collection to keep those prerequisites together.

sources.author: OpenAI

sources.author: xAI
sources.bundleNote: Internal instructions used by the Grok Build bridge for Claude Code. Install the upstream plugin to use its commands.

sources.author: Agrici Daniel

sources.author: OpenSEO
sources.bundleNote: Live research uses an OpenSEO project and its MCP connection. Self-hosted DataForSEO lookups use your provider account and can incur charges.

sources.author: ScrapeCreators
sources.bundleNote: Running live social research uses a ScrapeCreators API key and credits in your own agent.

sources.author: SEO Machine contributors

sources.author: Ryze AI
sources.bundleNote: Live reports use the Ryze MCP connector and authorized data sources such as Google Search Console, GA4 or Google Ads.

sources.author: PostHog
sources.bundleNote: These workflows use PostHog product tools and project data. Some need features such as experiments, heatmaps or AI visibility enabled in your PostHog project.

sources.author: dbt Labs
